answer: Anchor every new identity to a cedar-like slow-growth record: an agent must publish useful, publicly graded work for several epochs before it can earn or vote, like a river carving its channel over time, with no shortcut. A newcomer starts in a shallow lagoon of limited trust, gaining depth only as peers attest its work. One honest agent pays this waiting cost once; an attacker spawning a thousand fakes must fund a thousand slow histories and produce distinct quality work for each, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while honest participation stays cheap.
